quote: Just trying to get an estimate to be honest.
stewart_read: The interest reason was thin and the rep took it at face value without probing depth — no bill-pain or motivation was ever surfaced.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged further probing unnecessary since the customer was already cooperative and moving toward booking.
coaching_implication: A quick follow-up like 'what got you looking into it now?' could have surfaced a real motivator to anchor the appointment to.

quote: $1.80. And I actually do have my own power meter, it looks like.
stewart_read: Bill amount was captured but the rep pivoted immediately into an unrelated meter-wiring tangent rather than reflecting the bill back as a hook.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer himself changed the subject to the meter, so the rep may have simply followed the conversational thread rather than dropping the anchor.
coaching_implication: Even when the customer redirects, the rep should return to the bill number later in the call to tie it to the appointment's value.

quote: It's brand new. It's brand new.
stewart_read: A brand-new roof removes a common objection/DQ risk and is a positive qualification signal the rep captured but did not reinforce as a plus for the customer.
coaching_implication: Rep could note 'perfect, that roof will support this for decades' to build customer confidence in the fit.

quote: I am active duty. Yes. Navy.
stewart_read: Military status was captured for a discount qualifier, correctly acknowledged with a thank-you-for-service, a solid rapport touch.
coaching_implication: Good moment — the rep tied it to a tangible discount, which is the right move; no coaching needed here.

stewart_read: The rep offered tomorrow without an urgency anchor and had to iterate through two more days before landing a time — booking felt improvised rather than confidently anchored.
alternative_hypothesis: This could just be efficient real-time scheduling rather than a failure — the rep did land a specific day and time within a few exchanges.
coaching_implication: Leading with a firmer anchor ('let's get you on for this week while the estimate's fresh') would reduce back-and-forth.

quote: We've locked you out for an hour just so you don't feel rushed,
stewart_read: Button-up covered the hour-block and confirmation promise but never asked the verbal handshake ('is that fair?') or the no-driving/computer instruction.
coaching_implication: Add the explicit 'is that fair?' close and the no-driving/computer instruction — both are missing and both are tied to show-rate.
